maternal broccoli sprout consumption can prevent mammary tumor development in offspring through epigenetics.
the maternal consumption of broccoli sprouts (a rich source of sulforaphane), which is an epigenetic agent, can prevent the development of estrogen receptor-negative mammary tumors in the offspring.

maternal exposure to broccoli sprouts (BSp) can prevent the development of estrogen receptor ( ER ) negative tumors in offspring, and that this prevention is associated with changes in the epigenetic status of the tumors, which is linked with changes in the expression of tumor-related genes.

the potential of maternal exposure to dietary BSp on the prevention of ER-negative breast cancer and the underlying molecular mechanism of action.

maternal broccoli sprout exposure can be a potential dietary strategy to prevent ER-negative mammary cancer in their offspring through the modulation of epigenetic alterations.

the consumption of cruciferous vegetables, especially broccoli sprouts, by mothers during their pregnancy or breastfeeding periods can be an effective strategy to protect their offspring from breast cancer.
